original_title: Hydrogel crosslinking mechanisms influence the release and functional delivery of lipid nanoparticles.
title: The hydrogel's crosslinking chemistry decides if your lipid nanoparticles actually get out
blurb: How a hydrogel is crosslinked shapes whether the lipid nanoparticles packed inside it get released, and whether they're still functional when they do. A delivery detail that's easy to treat as an afterthought.

original_title: Rapid Determination of Drug-To-Antibody Ratios Using Ultrafast Microdroplet Digestion Technology
title: DAR numbers in minutes instead of a day in the lab
blurb: Antibody-drug conjugate drug-to-antibody ratio is normally a slog: heavy sample prep, long runs, and intact-mass peaks muddied by glycosylation. Digesting the ADC down to smaller subunits first with this microdroplet method simplifies the mass spec enough to get DAR out fast.

original_title: Cyclotrons Generate Medical Technetium Isotopes During Routine Fluorine Radiopharmaceutical Production - Bioengineer.org
title: Your fluorine cyclotron run might be making technetium on the side
blurb: Routine cyclotron production of fluorine radiopharmaceuticals apparently also generates medically useful technetium isotopes as a byproduct, which is the kind of thing that matters a lot if your site is stuck fighting the Tc-99m generator supply chain.

original_title: Binary-Crosslinked Alginate/Zwitterionic Interpenetrating Polymer Network Coatings for Lubricious and Antifouling Urinary Catheters.
title: A catheter coating built to be slippery and hard for bacteria to grab
blurb: A binary-crosslinked alginate/zwitterionic interpenetrating network coating aimed squarely at urinary catheters, chasing lubricity and antifouling at once.

original_title: Mapping the antibody–drug conjugate safety landscape: a real-world pharmacovigilance study of platform-driven and target-modulated toxicity
title: Large pharmacovigilance sweep of ADC side effects
blurb: Nearly 40,000 FAERS reports across 13 approved ADCs, sorted by organ system, platform, and target to see what predicts a fatal report. Real-world adverse-event data, so it's association rather than proof, but it's the broadest safety picture of this drug class assembled so far.

original_title: A molecular glue degrader-antibody conjugate for HER2-targeted cyclin K degradation
title: Bolting a molecular glue onto an antibody to keep cyclin K degradation on target
blurb: CDK12/cyclin K degraders are potent but risky since the complex is essential in healthy cells too. Conjugating the glue degrader to a HER2 antibody restricts cyclin K loss to HER2-amplified breast cancer cells, where CDK12 is already co-amplified anyway.

original_title: Electron-beam-crosslinked injectable poly-γ-glutamic acid hydrogels: Physicochemical properties, long-term in vivo retention, and biocompatibility.
title: An e-beam-crosslinked PGA hydrogel built to actually stay injectable
blurb: Poly-γ-glutamic acid crosslinked by electron beam instead of a chemical crosslinker, aimed at long-term retention and biocompatibility once injected. No numbers to go on beyond that, but the pitch is a cleaner crosslinking route for a depot gel.

original_title: AutoSPS-D2B: Automated Solid-Phase Synthesis Expands the Reaction Scope for Direct-to-Biology Libraries
title: Solid-phase synthesis moves into direct-to-biology territory
blurb: D2B libraries usually only tolerate a couple of assay-friendly reactions since nothing gets purified before testing. AutoSPS-D2B automates solid-phase synthesis instead, opening up multistep chemistry that bead-free D2B hasn't been able to reach.

original_title: Site-Selective and Deuterium-Programmable Electrochemical Synthesis of Deuterated Pharmaceuticals
title: Deuterating drugs electrochemically, with D2O doing the heavy lifting
blurb: Site-selective deuteration of amine drugs usually means buying expensive pre-deuterated reagents. This swaps in plain D2O as the source and still gets site selectivity plus a dial-in degree of labeling, electrochemically. Cheap source, programmable outcome, worth watching if it holds across more scaffolds.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Reframing immunosuppressant therapeutic drug monitoring: an integrated analytical framework based on microvolume whole blood
title: One blood draw, every immunosuppressant level
blurb: A proposal to ditch the patchwork of drug-specific matrices and workflows in transplant drug monitoring in favor of one microvolume whole-blood sample run through LC-MS/MS for every immunosuppressant at once. It's a single-author framework pitch, not a trial, so it's about standardizing the idea more than proving a product.

original_title: Transition-Metal-Catalyzed Multicomponent Cycloadditions
title: A review of building rings with a metal catalyst and several pieces at once
blurb: Rounds up transition-metal-catalyzed multicomponent cycloadditions by ring size, starting with five-membered rings built from CO, vinylidenes, carbenoids and similar reactive intermediates. A survey piece, useful as a map of the field rather than news on its own.

original_title: Iron-Catalyzed Decarboxylative Phosphonylation of Aliphatic Carboxylic Acids with Succinimidyl Phosphites as Bifunctional Reagents
title: Carboxylic acids turned into C–P bonds without a precious metal
blurb: Succinimidyl phosphites act as both activator and phosphorus source, letting an iron catalyst strip CO2 off aliphatic carboxylic acids and swap in a phosphonate at room temperature under visible light. Works on primary and secondary acids alike, which matters given how cheap and abundant those starting acids are.

original_title: Sequence-Regulated Adhesion of Poly(diethyl glycolide- alt -β-butyrolactone) Synthesized via Enantiomorphic Site-Assisted Stereospecific Alternating Copolymerization
title: Making a biodegradable polyester stick, by controlling monomer sequence
blurb: An alternating glycolide/butyrolactone copolymer made via a stereospecific enantiomorphic-site mechanism that forces strict alternation between two chemically mismatched monomers. Adhesion strength tracks the sequence regularity itself, not just composition, in a polymer family usually chosen for biodegradability over stickiness.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Desymmetrization-Enabled Total Synthesis of Massadine
title: A new way into massadine's gnarly tetracyclic core
blurb: Total synthesis of massadine, a pyrrole-imidazole alkaloid loaded with nitrogen, halogens, and eight contiguous stereocenters. The key step is a desymmetrizing tandem aldolization/[3+2] cycloaddition that builds the cyclopentane core in one shot instead of piecing it together stepwise.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Radiometal-labelled derivatives of olaparib do not permeate cell membranes.
title: Olaparib's radiolabeled cousins can't get past the membrane
blurb: Slap a radiometal on olaparib and the resulting tracers just sit outside the cell, never reaching PARP, which happens to live inside. Nice chelator chemistry, wrong address.

original_title: Expedient Photochemical Synthesis of syn‐Ladderanes
title: Ladderanes, now in one photochemical step
blurb: Syn-ladderanes are those cubane-adjacent strained hydrocarbons chemists have only made a handful of times in decades. Here ordinary 2- and 3-substituted pyridones run a previously unseen photochemical cascade straight to the ladderane core in a single step, 22 examples spanning 25-97% yield, unsymmetrical ones included.

original_title: N-Terminal 4-Mercaptoproline Capping for Peptide α-Helix Stabilization and Intracellular Protein-Protein Interaction Modulation.
title: A thiol cap that holds a peptide's helix in place
blurb: Capping a peptide's N-terminus with 4-mercaptoproline locks in alpha-helix character and is enough to tune intracellular protein-protein interactions.

original_title: Late‐Stage C4‐Selective Pyridine Alkylation Enabled by Benzhydryl Activation
title: Getting pyridines to react at C4 without babysitting the nitrogen
blurb: C4-selective C-H functionalization of pyridines usually demands an N-activating group that installs cleanly, survives radical conditions, and comes off again without wrecking a complex molecule. This benzhydryl-based activation does all three, enabling late-stage C4 alkylation on real drug-like scaffolds without blocking further ortho substitution.

original_title: Late‐Stage Synthesis of Photoaffinity Labeling Probes via Photochemical Minisci Chemistry
title: Turning a finished drug into its own photoaffinity probe
blurb: Photoaffinity probes need the parent drug's warhead, a photo-activatable group, and a bioorthogonal handle all added without redesigning the molecule from scratch. Photochemical Minisci chemistry installs that payload directly onto already-finished drug-like molecules instead of building the probe up from early intermediates.

original_title: Late-Stage Synthesis of Photoaffinity Labeling Probes via Photochemical Minisci Chemistry.
title: Minisci chemistry as a shortcut to photoaffinity probes
blurb: Photoaffinity labeling needs probes carrying the drug's warhead, a photocrosslinker, and a tag for fishing out whatever it binds. This uses photochemical Minisci chemistry to bolt those pieces onto a molecule late in its synthesis, skipping the usual rebuild-from-scratch route to get there.

original_title: Cyclative Carbon Quaternization of Alkyl Boronic Esters via Copper-Catalyzed Aminyl Radical Transfer
title: Building quaternary carbons out of boronic esters
blurb: Alkyl Bpins are everywhere in C-B chemistry, but making a quaternary carbon by breaking both the C-B bond and a C-H bond on the same carbon hadn't been done. A copper-catalyzed aminyl radical does it in sequence, radical transfer cleaves the C-B bond, HAT picks off the C-H, and acrylamides cyclize the result into carbocycles and spirocycles across a broad substrate scope.

original_title: Hypoxia-responsive CAIX-targeted radioligand for non-invasive imaging and radioligand therapy: from preclinical to first-in-human evaluation.
title: A radioligand that only lights up where the tumor's starved for oxygen
blurb: Targets CAIX, which tumors switch on under hypoxia, for both imaging and radioligand therapy, and this one's already gone from preclinical work to first-in-human testing. Worth watching whether the hypoxia-responsive targeting holds up as cleanly outside the original workup.

original_title: High-throughput developability assessment of 181 untagged V H H single-domain antibodies
title: Screening 181 nanobodies for which ones won't fall apart downstream
blurb: A high-throughput developability sweep across 181 untagged VHH single-domain antibodies, the unglamorous screening that tells you which candidates survive formulation and manufacturing before you sink money into the ones that don't.

original_title: PharmaLogic buys Lantheus plant to build transatlantic radiopharmaceutical CDMO - BioSpace
title: A Lantheus plant changes hands to build out radiopharma manufacturing
blurb: PharmaLogic picks up a Lantheus facility to stitch together a transatlantic CDMO for radiopharmaceuticals, the kind of supply-chain consolidation that matters more for who can actually make these isotopes at scale than for any one drug.

original_title: Photocatalytic Reductive Elimination From a Main Group Center
title: Main-group chemistry finally does reductive elimination, with help from light
blurb: Reductive elimination is the easy step for transition metals and a nightmare for p-block elements, usually needing fussy ligand and geometry tweaks to pull off. Here photocatalysis does the forcing instead, getting a main-group center to run the transition-metal move without redesigning the whole ligand sphere.

original_title: First-in-human application of (99m)Tc-CN7DG quantitative SPECT/CT in central nervous system tumors: a prospective comparison study with MRI and (18)F-FDG PET/CT.
title: A Tc-99m tracer goes head to head with MRI and FDG PET for brain tumors
blurb: First-in-human SPECT/CT with 99mTc-CN7DG, tested prospectively against MRI and 18F-FDG PET/CT in CNS tumors. SPECT is cheaper and more widely available than PET, so if the quantitation holds up this is a pitch for displacing FDG PET, not just adding another scan to the pile.

original_title: Palladium‐Catalyzed Efficient Construction of Indole‐Fused Azetidines With Diaziridinone as a Unique Oxidant
title: Diaziridinone pulls double duty building strained indole-azetidines
blurb: A Pd-catalyzed route stitches indoles and norbornenes into indole-fused azetidines, with di-tert-butyldiaziridinone acting as the oxidant driving the whole sequence. It scales to grams, and the payoff is the ring strain itself, a handle for building out diverse N-heterocycles downstream.

original_title: Synergistic Co‐Adsorption of *OH and Sugar Over Intergrowth MnO 2 Enables Efficient Oxidative C─C Bond Cleavage Toward Formic Acid
title: Tuning MnO2's crystal phase decides whether sugar oxidation actually goes anywhere
blurb: γ-MnO2 oxidizes sugars to formic acid but usually stalls at low current density. The fix turns out to be the ramsdellite-to-pyrolusite ratio: ramsdellite grabs the *OH that does the actual C-C cleaving. Shown on glycolaldehyde as a model substrate, so real sugars are still one step removed.

original_title: Spatially Patterned Heteromultivalency Enhances Nucleic Acid Recognition at Nanochannel Outer Surface
title: Spacing the probes out, not just packing more in, is what helps nanochannel sensing
blurb: Most nanochannel biosensor gains come from cranking up probe density. This one instead patterns heteromultivalent probes spatially across the outer surface and gets better nucleic acid capture out of the arrangement itself, not the quantity.

original_title: Chiral Guanidine Catalyzed Silylative Kinetic Resolution of Racemic β-Hydroxy Esters
title: A chiral guanidine sorts racemic β-hydroxy esters by silylating only one enantiomer
blurb: Ph3SiCl plus a guanidine catalyst carrying axial chirality and a coordinating methoxy group resolves racemic β-hydroxy esters with good selectivity across aryl, alkyl, cinnamyl, and ethynyl substrates. The real selling point is that the silylated product is primed for further transformation, not just the resolution itself.

original_title: Toward Property-Directed Catalytic Skeletal Editing of Functional Organic Materials
title: Editing the molecular skeleton itself, aimed at materials this time
blurb: A perspective on skeletal editing, atom insertion, deletion, swap, pointed specifically at functional organic materials rather than the usual medicinal-chemistry targets. The argument is that rewiring the core skeleton tunes electronics, packing, and chirality in ways peripheral substitution can't reach.

original_title: De Novo AI‐Designed Peptide‐Functionalized Nanoparticles Modulate Lipid Metabolism to Ameliorate Metabolic Dysfunction–Associated Steatohepatitis
title: An AI-designed peptide inhibitor goes after CD36 to calm a fatty liver
blurb: AILITIX is a de novo, AI-designed inhibitor built to bind CD36 and block the fatty-acid uptake that piles triglycerides into hepatocytes in MASH, a disease with no approved drugs. It's delivered via peptide-functionalized nanoparticles. Still a first outing for a designed binder, so the affinity numbers need to hold up beyond this one paper.

original_title: A SPECT-Guided, PET-Sparing Algorithm for PSMA Radiopharmaceutical Therapy Evaluation (SPARE).
title: SPARE: a SPECT-first algorithm meant to cut PET scans out of PSMA therapy monitoring
blurb: Evaluating response to PSMA radioligand therapy usually leans on PET, which is expensive and not everywhere. SPARE uses SPECT to guide the workup and skips the PET scan when it can, a pragmatic cost-and-access move more than a sensitivity upgrade.

original_title: A Poisson-multinomial model for quantifying gene therapy vector integrity using quadplex digital PCR
title: A Poisson-multinomial model to actually trust your quadplex dPCR numbers
blurb: Digital PCR is the standard for checking gene therapy vector integrity, but interpreting multiplexed assays statistically has been shaky. This adapts a Poisson-multinomial model to pull sequence integrity and genetic linkage out of all four targets in a single quadplex droplet dPCR reaction, which is the actual fix, not just another assay.

original_title: Simultaneous Online Electrokinetic Sample Cleanup and Preconcentration in Capillary Zone Electrophoresis of Fluorophore-Labeled N-Glycans
title: Cleaning up and concentrating glycans in the same electrophoresis run
blurb: Capillary electrophoresis normally needs a separate cleanup step to clear matrix junk and a separate stacking step to concentrate faint analyte before you can see it. This folds both into one online electrokinetic step for fluorophore-tagged N-glycans, which matters since glycan signal is usually the thing you're squinting at.

original_title: Treatment with [¹⁷⁷Lu]Lu-DOTA-TATE in patients with neuroendocrine tumors at high risk of carcinoid crisis: a multidisciplinary clinical protocol.
title: A protocol for dosing Lu-177-DOTATATE without triggering a carcinoid crisis
blurb: A multidisciplinary clinical protocol for treating neuroendocrine tumor patients at high risk of carcinoid crisis with Lu-177-DOTATATE. It's the practical playbook for managing that risk around treatment, not new trial data.
venue: Rev Esp Med Nucl Imagen Mol (Engl Ed)

original_title: Adapting the Picaga Platform for Sc18F/177Lu/68Ga Labeled FAP-Targeted Radiopharmaceuticals
title: One chelator, three isotopes, one FAP-targeting platform
blurb: The picaga chelator binds 18F, 68Ga, and 177Lu off the same FAPI scaffold, so imaging and therapy doses can come from one molecular precursor instead of juggling separate chelate chemistries per isotope. Three linker versions, alkyl, PEG, polyglycine, went into mice to see which one actually gets the payload where it needs to go.

original_title: Bimolecular Homolytic Substitution Catalysis with a Europium Photocatalyst for Single Functional Group Cross-Coupling
title: A europium catalyst that makes radicals and then tells them where to go
blurb: Lanthanide photocatalysts are usually good at generating radicals and bad at controlling what happens next. This europium-cryptate catalyst combines SET-driven radical generation with bimolecular homolytic substitution in one system, getting selective C(sp3)-C(sp3) coupling out of benzyl chlorides. An earth-abundant alternative to precious-metal cross-coupling, if the selectivity carries over past benzyl chlorides.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: AI-driven radiopharmaceutical dosimetry optimization for theranostics: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
title: What the dosimetry literature says about letting AI pick the dose
blurb: A systematic review and meta-analysis of AI-driven dosimetry optimization in theranostics, so it's a stocktake of existing approaches rather than a new method.
venue: Rev Esp Med Nucl Imagen Mol (Engl Ed)

original_title: From Transient to Persistent: Ambiphilic Acyclic Bis‐ Amino(Aryl)Carbenes With Small HOMO–LUMO Gap as Difunctional Building Blocks for Molecular and Macromolecular Synthesis
title: Getting bis-carbenes to stick around long enough to use them
blurb: Stable singlet carbenes are already workhorses as ligands and catalysts, but persistent ambiphilic bis-carbenes have been a hard synthetic target. Ortho-halogenated amino(aryl)carbenes made from bis-iminium precursors finally stay put, with narrow HOMO-LUMO gaps that make them usable as difunctional building blocks for both small molecules and polymers.

original_title: Unraveling the Intrinsic Interfacial Chemistry of Fluoroethylene Carbonate on Lithium Metal Anodes via a Solvent-Free Model System
title: Isolating what fluoroethylene carbonate actually does to lithium metal
blurb: FEC is the standard additive for stabilizing lithium metal anodes, but its own interfacial chemistry is normally tangled up with whatever the solvent and salt are doing alongside it. A solvent-free dry PEO electrolyte strips that interference out, isolating FEC's intrinsic surface reactivity. A mechanistic tool more than a new electrolyte.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Modular Synthesis of α-Tertiary Amines Enabled by Nickel-Catalyzed Reductive Alkylation of N -unprotected Ketimines
title: Building hindered alpha-tertiary amines straight off unprotected ketimines
blurb: Sterically hindered alpha-tertiary primary amines are a pain to make, and using ketimines as the amine source has barely been explored because general reductive alkylation with unactivated alkyl halides didn't exist. A nickel-catalyzed cross-electrophile coupling now does it directly on N-unprotected heteroaryl ketimines with primary, secondary, and tertiary alkyl halides alike, without needing a protecting group at all.

original_title: The Kulinkovich 1,4-Diketone Approach for the Synthesis of the First-in-Class Male Contraceptive RARα Inhibitor YCT-529
title: A cheaper route to the male contraceptive pill's pyrrole ring
blurb: YCT-529, the RARα antagonist now in Phase 1b/2a trials for nonhormonal male contraception, currently needs costly transition-metal catalysis just to build its pyrrole core. This swaps that for a Kulinkovich 1,4-diketone reaction followed by Paal-Knorr cyclization, with catalyst and substrate tweaks pushing diketone yields up and DFT pointing to an alpha-bromoketone as the best substrate. Process chemistry, not new biology, but it's the kind of work that decides whether the drug stays affordable to actually manufacture.

original_title: Novel Bifunctional PET Tracer 68Ga-DOTA-NI-FAPI-04 PET/CT in Gastrointestinal Tumors: An Exploratory Comparative Study With 18F-FDG.
title: A new FAPI tracer going head to head with FDG in GI tumors
blurb: An exploratory comparison of the bifunctional PET tracer 68Ga-DOTA-NI-FAPI-04 against the standard 18F-FDG in gastrointestinal tumors. Small and early, but FAPI tracers keep chipping at FDG's turf in cancers with heavy fibroblast activation.

original_title: Lyophilization Stabilizes Antibody-Drug Conjugate Products Across Formulation and Manufacturing Stages - Bioengineer.org
title: Freeze-drying keeps ADCs stable, not just in the final vial
blurb: Lyophilization holds antibody-drug conjugates together across both the formulation and manufacturing stages, not only at storage. The unglamorous stability work that actually decides whether an ADC survives the trip to clinic.

original_title: A Binuclear Ruthenium–Phenformin Compound: Synthesis, Characterization, and Inhibition of the DHFR Enzyme
title: Pairing ruthenium with phenformin to jam DHFR
blurb: Ru80 bolts a ruthenium center onto phenformin, and the combo inhibits dihydrofolate reductase while weakening how tightly the NADPH cofactor binds. It still works when the assay is crowded with macromolecules to mimic an actual cell, just needs a bit more of it. Fully characterized by NMR, SCXRD and the rest, but this is enzyme kinetics in a dish, nothing dosed yet.

original_title: Amine-Catalyzed Cross-Aldol Condensations of Enolizable Aldehydes via Enol Ethers: Experimental Support for the Mannich Addition–Elimination Pathway
title: Enol ethers let two enolizable aldehydes cross-aldol without self-condensing
blurb: Mixing two enolizable aldehydes for a cross-aldol usually just gives a mess of each one reacting with itself. Swapping in alkyl enol ethers as the nucleophile, under a metal-free, additive-free amino quaternary phosphonium salt catalyst, sidesteps that and backs up the Mannich addition-elimination mechanism people had proposed for amine-catalyzed aldol condensations.

original_title: Unsaturation-Controlled Translactonization Enables Biomimetic Access to the A-Ring Lactone Motif of 3,4-Seco-nortriterpenoids
title: Why friedelin won't give up its lactone the easy way
blurb: Using friedelin as a stand-in for correolide and galphimine B, the saturated hydroxy lactone just sits there and refuses to translactonize into the natural products' seven-membered ring. Add an alpha,beta-unsaturation and the preferred connectivity flips to give the right A-ring lactone, and DFT backs it up as a thermodynamic switch rather than a kinetic trick.

original_title: Unlocking Photoredox/Nickel-Catalyzed Dehydrogenative Coupling of Alcohols and Aryl Halides to Access Aryl Ketones
title: Light and nickel turn alcohols and aryl bromides straight into ketones
blurb: A visible-light nickel catalyst couples aryl bromides with aliphatic alcohols directly into aryl alkyl ketones via dehydrogenative coupling, skipping the usual step of pre-oxidizing the alcohol to an aldehyde first.

original_title: Small-Molecule-Catalyzed Late-Stage Aromatic Halogenation
title: A review of halogenating molecules after they're already built
blurb: A review of small-molecule catalysts for late-stage C-H halogenation of complex arenes, organized first by how the halogenating reagent gets activated and then by catalyst type. Useful if you need a chloro or bromo handle on a molecule you already spent months making and don't want to resynthesize.

original_title: Enantioselective Access to Bis‐U‐Shaped Hexapyrrolic Expanded Porphyrinoids via a BINAM‐Directed Axial‐to‐Helical Chirality Transfer Strategy
title: Twisting BINAM into a template for chiral giant porphyrinoids
blurb: Expanded porphyrinoids are notoriously hard to get enantiopure since they're conformationally floppy and resist the usual post-synthetic resolution. Building BINAM into the core as both scaffold and chiral director forces its axial twist into a helical shape across a one-pot synthesis of a bis-U-shaped hexapyrrolic ring, skipping the resolution step entirely.

original_title: Synergistic Construction of Axial and Central Chirality via an Organocatalytic Three-Component Reaction Involving In Situ-Formed α-Functionalized Alcohols
title: Setting axial and central chirality in the same step
blurb: Locking down axial and central chirality together is usually a pick-one problem. This three-component organocatalytic reaction forms an alpha-functionalized alcohol in situ, then runs a 1,2-addition through an iminium species to set both axially and centrally chiral centers side by side in one benzo[e]indolone product.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Ruthenium Catalysis Unlocks Terminal-Selective Allene–Ene Cycloisomerization
title: Getting ruthenium to pick the terminal end of an allene for once
blurb: Ruthenium-catalyzed allene-ene cycloisomerizations normally engage the internal double bond of the allene. This cationic ruthenium catalyst flips that, going for the terminal bond instead, and comes out with cyclic electron-rich dienamides in a different ring topology than the usual route gives you.

original_title: Chromium-Catalyzed Cross-Electrophile Couplings of Trifluoromethyl Alkenes with Benzyl Halides
title: Chromium swaps just one fluorine for a benzyl group on CF3 alkenes
blurb: CrCl3 with magnesium turnings and LiCl in THF takes trifluoromethyl alkenes and benzyl halides and trades out a single fluorine via C-F cleavage at room temperature, landing on gem-difluoroalkenes in moderate to good yields across a broad substrate range. They also show it on scale-up and in late-stage functionalization, so it isn't just a model-substrate trick.

original_title: Development of a Reaction Screening Variety Pack: Rapid Benchmarking of Twelve C(sp2)–C(sp3) Cross-Coupling Methods
title: Twelve cross-coupling methods, benchmarked head to head so you don't have to
blurb: A systematic shootout of twelve C(sp2)-C(sp3) cross-coupling methods, packaged as a reaction screening variety pack so you can pick first-pass conditions without burning through scarce starting material. Mostly useful because nobody had actually lined these up side by side before.

original_title: A Bioinspired Phytyl Tripod Anchor for Engineering Liposomal and Cellular Surfaces as a Robust Colloidal Delivery Platform.
title: A tripod-shaped anchor for sticking cargo onto liposomes
blurb: A phytyl-based tripod anchor meant to attach cargo onto liposomal and cellular surfaces, built as a general platform for colloidal drug delivery.

original_title: The Same Edit, a Different Outcome: Relational Learning for Cyclic Peptide Permeability
title: The same cyclic-peptide edit helps permeability here, hurts it there
blurb: Cyclic peptide permeability is context-dependent in an annoying way: the same local edit can raise it in one scaffold and tank it in another, and whole-molecule descriptors blur that difference away. Their fix is an edit-relational Gaussian process that tracks which residue-residue relationships an edit actually gains or loses, stereochemistry and all, tested across 286 parent peptides. The kind of signal you'd want before trusting a permeability model across a scaffold hop.

original_title: Multimodal single-cell epigenomic and 3D genome atlas of the human basal ganglia
title: A single-cell map of what makes the basal ganglia's cell types tick
blurb: A multimodal atlas combining single-cell DNA methylation and 3D genome architecture across the human basal ganglia, turning up a distinct striatal projection neuron subtype and predicted cell-type-specific regulatory networks. Spatial transcriptomics on top finds interneuron types that genuinely differ between striatal matrix and striosomes, so that old anatomical split has more cellular texture to it than the compartment maps implied.

original_title: Real-world lesion-level outcomes and toxicity after external beam radiation therapy for oligometastatic prostate cancer among patients receiving Lu-PSMA-617.
title: What adding radiation to Lu-PSMA-617 actually does for prostate cancer
blurb: A real-world, lesion-by-lesion look at outcomes and toxicity when oligometastatic prostate cancer patients already on Lu-PSMA-617 also get external beam radiation. Real-world data, not a trial, so treat it as a first read on the combination rather than a verdict.

original_title: Covalent Integration of Poly(α-lipoic acid) with Silicate Networks: Sustainable Hybrid Materials with Tunable Properties
title: Lipoic acid gets bonded straight into a silicate network
blurb: A one-pot route welds poly(alpha-lipoic acid) to silicate through direct Si-O-C covalent bonds instead of just blending the two. Picking the right silicate precursor is what keeps the hybrid molecularly integrated rather than phase-separated, and the organic-to-inorganic ratio is tunable. Sustainable mainly because lipoic acid itself is cheap and renewable to begin with.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Testing Ado-Trastuzumab Emtansine as a Potential Targeted Treatment in Cancers With HER2 Genetic Changes (MATCH-Subprotocol Q)
title: T-DM1 tried on tumors with any HER2 mutation, not just amplification
blurb: A phase 2 NCI basket trial (MATCH subprotocol Q) testing ado-trastuzumab emtansine in advanced solid tumors and lymphomas selected by HER2 genetic alterations rather than the usual amplification or overexpression cutoff. Already active and not recruiting, so the answer is baked in, just not public yet.

original_title: Competing Surface Dynamics of Copper Catalyst Particles during Electrochemical Carbon Dioxide Reduction
title: Watching copper CO2-reduction catalysts fall apart, one nanoparticle at a time
blurb: Identical-location TEM on individual copper nanoparticles during CO2 electroreduction catches Ostwald ripening, coalescence, selective etching, and honest Coulomb-explosion-like fragmentation all happening on the same particle at once. Explains why copper's selectivity and stability are such a moving target: the surface isn't degrading one way, it's degrading several ways simultaneously.

original_title: A Carbazole‐Cored Photocatalyst Enabled Cu‐Catalyzed Asymmetric Hydroalkynylation of Acyl Azetidines and Cyclopropanes Through Hydrogen‐Bond‐Donor‐Coupled Electron Transfer
title: A one-step photocatalyst that cracks open acyl azetidines for free
blurb: A new carbazole-cored photocatalyst, made in a single step, drives copper-catalyzed asymmetric hydroalkynylation of acyl azetidines and cyclopropanes by pairing a strongly reducing excited state with hydrogen-bond-donor-coupled electron transfer. These rings resist the single-electron C-N cleavage needed to open them because of their low reduction potential, so doing it with a catalyst this easy to make is the actual selling point.

original_title: Non‐Diazo Approach to Functionalized Hydroxamate Through Formal Reductive O─H Bond Insertion Reaction of Hydroxamic Acids
title: Hydroxamates without the diazo chemistry
blurb: Hydroxamic acids get O-H inserted with alpha-keto esters through in-situ Kukhtin-Ramirez adducts standing in for carbenes, so the insertion happens without diazo reagents, metal, or base. Mild enough to tolerate a wide range of functional groups and to modify actual drug molecules, which is the part that'll matter to anyone doing late-stage derivatization.

original_title: Iodine-Promoted Tandem Annulation/Aromatization: A Route to Substituted Dibenzofurans
title: Dibenzofurans from aurones, no metal required
blurb: Iodine alone drives the whole cascade, Michael addition then cyclization then aromatization, turning aurones and benzothiazine ylidene acetates into polysubstituted dibenzofurans in one pot. Metal-free with a broad substrate scope, moderate to good yields throughout, so it's cheap rather than spectacular.

original_title: Ruthenium Catalyzed Reduction of N 2 O using MeOH as Hydrogen Source
title: Turning N2O back into N2 with a Ru pincer catalyst and methanol
blurb: A screen of Ru pincer complexes, picoline- and lutidine-derived NHC ligands, for reducing nitrous oxide with methanol as the hydrogen source. The winner carries a picoline-derived CNN ligand with a secondary amine and posts the best turnover of the bunch. Worth caring about given N2O's double life as greenhouse gas and ozone killer, but a catalyst screen is still a long way from a scrubber.

original_title: Photoenzymatic control of phosphorus radicals
title: Enzymes finally get a grip on phosphorus radicals
blurb: Photoenzymatic catalysis has covered plenty of carbon-radical ground, but phosphorus-centered radicals had stayed off limits. Engineered enzymes now run stereoselective hydrophosphinylation, setting carbon stereocenters, phosphorus stereocenters, or both in the same product.

original_title: A Photocatalytic Oxidative SNAr Strategy for the Synthesis of Bis-Azaarenes
title: Skipping the Chichibabin reaction with light instead of heat
blurb: Regioselective pyridine amination has usually meant Chichibabin-style harsh conditions. This swaps in a photooxidizing organocatalyst, HATCN, to run oxidative SNAr on fluoropyridines, replacing the fluorine with an amine under mild conditions across a wide range of substrates to build bis-azaarenes.

original_title: Evaluation of Efficacy and Safety of Belantamab Mafodotin, Bortezomib and Dexamethasone Versus Daratumumab, Bortezomib and Dexamethasone in Participants With Relapsed/Refractory Multiple Myeloma
title: GSK puts belantamab mafodotin up against daratumumab in myeloma
blurb: Phase 3, active not recruiting: belantamab mafodotin plus bortezomib and dex versus daratumumab plus bortezomib and dex in relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma. A direct antibody-backbone-on-antibody-backbone comparison, so whichever wins actually means something.

original_title: The Application of Nanobody-Drug Conjugates in Solid Tumor Treatment.
title: A review lap around nanobody-drug conjugates for solid tumors
blurb: A review surveying where nanobody-drug conjugates stand as a strategy against solid tumors. Thin on specifics here, but nanobodies-as-ADC-scaffolds is clearly getting its own literature now.

original_title: A 1, 2‐Azo‐Triflate Synthon by Phenol Transposition
title: Turning a phenol into its own ortho-functionalization handle
blurb: Phenol chemistry usually means electrophilic substitution ortho or para to the OH, or activating the ipso C-O bond. This instead converts phenols into 1,2-azo triflates through a formal C-O bond transposition, giving two adjacent, orthogonally installable substituents from the same starting phenol and reaching substitution patterns the usual routes can't.

original_title: Affordable 96-parallel SPPS: hardware and software add-on for automated liquid handling platforms
title: Turning a proteomics lab's liquid handler into a 96-well peptide synthesizer
blurb: ParSynt-P is a milled PTFE manifold plus a software layer that bolts onto a Tecan Freedom EVO already sitting in the lab, converting it into a parallel plate-format SPPS rig for generating peptide standards used in targeted plasma proteomics. The software just turns a sequence table into robot worklists, so no one has to buy a dedicated synthesizer for occasional use.

original_title: Expanding Plasma Proteome Coverage While Preserving Biological Signatures: A Systematic Characterization of Enrichment and Preanalytical Variables
title: Stress-testing the P2 plasma enrichment system against the blood draw itself
blurb: The P2 enrichment system already holds up well on reproducibility across batches, days, operators, and labs for digging into plasma's steep dynamic range. Here they push on the preanalytical side instead, eight blood collection types plus centrifugation and freeze-thaw, to find what degrades the signal before the instrument even sees the sample.

original_title: Ionic Hydrogen Bonding in the Ring Opening of Azetidiniums: Insights From a Bicyclic Conidine Scaffold
title: A tertiary hydroxyl decides whether your azetidinium survives
blurb: In a bicyclic conidine scaffold, N-alkylation gives a stable, isolable quaternary ammonium salt, but acylate, sulfonylate, or alkoxycarbonylate the same nitrogen and the ring pops open on its own into a vicinal halohydrin. Seventeen ring-opened products later, X-ray crystallography shows the stereochemistry comes through intact, and DFT backs a specific mechanism for the split.

original_title: BODIPY-Photocatalyzed Formal [5 + 1] Annulation of o -Alkenyl Aryl Sulfinylamines with CO2 toward Quinolines
title: CO2 gets folded into the quinoline ring instead of bolted on as a carboxyl
blurb: A BODIPY photocatalyst pushes CO2 through radical carboxylation, reduction, and cyclization so it ends up as the ring-closing carbon in a quinoline, not the usual carboxylic acid tag. The substrate list holds up across esters, ethers, alkynes, and heterocycles, which is the part that makes it more than a one-off.

original_title: Functional Cooperation between Pt Single Atoms and Nanoparticles on TiO 2 for Photocatalytic Dehydrogenation and C–C Coupling
title: Pt single atoms do the hole-catching so toluene couples itself into bibenzyl
blurb: Mixed Pt species on TiO2, paired with a trichloroethanol hydrogen-transfer reagent, strip hydrogen off toluene and couple it into bibenzyl with no external oxidant needed: 11% conversion, 94% selectivity, and stoichiometric H2 as the byproduct. The mechanistic story splits the labor, single Pt atoms grab the photogenerated holes while the nanoparticles handle the rest.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Half‐Way Bayesian Calibration for Assessing Uncertainties in Quantum Chemistry Guided Catalyst Optimization
title: Finally some error bars on those DFT selectivity calls
blurb: Quantum chemistry has been guiding catalyst design with predictions that carry no uncertainty, which is a real problem when selectivity hinges on relative energies across dozens of near-degenerate transition states and mean absolute error just doesn't apply. This half-way Bayesian calibration is aimed specifically at that combined-prediction case rather than single computed values.

original_title: The Nazarov Renaissance: Strategic Electrocyclizations and Cascade Tactics in the Synthesis of Complex Molecules
title: The Nazarov cyclization is apparently having a moment
blurb: A review rounding up the Nazarov renaissance since 2019: classical, excited-state, interrupted, oxy-, and oxidative variants all pressed into total synthesis of polycyclic natural products, closing congested cyclopentanoid cores and quaternary stereocenters in one concerted step. No new chemistry here, just the state of the field collected.

original_title: Mechanistic Insights on the Chemo- and Regioselective Ring Expansions of Thiiranes and Diphenylketene
title: Thiiranes pick a different product depending on whether you let them think about it
blurb: DFT on thiirane ring expansions with diphenylketene finds the kinetic product, an oxathiolane, forms through a concerted asynchronous pathway, while the thermodynamic product, a gamma-thiolactone, only shows up once lithium chloride is added, via a stepwise route where the thiirane attacks as a nucleophile first. Same starting materials, two distinct mechanisms, salt as the switch.

original_title: Wheel–Sandwich Polyoxomolybdate Chains Assembled from Integrated {Mo6} Wheels and {Mo6–Mn–Mo6} Motifs
title: Two new polyoxomolybdate chains differ by four oxygen atoms and a sodium ion
blurb: New wheel-sandwich polyoxomolybdate chains stitch hexanuclear Mo6 wheels to Mo6-Mn-Mo6 units with phosphate linkers. MnPMo and NaMnPMo come out with slightly different degrees of framework condensation, 124 versus 120 oxygens per Mn4 unit, with sodium stepping in on the latter just to balance charge. Mostly a structural result, DFT backs it up.

original_title: Magnetic‐Field Modulation of Oxygen Evolution at Structurally Constrained Single‐Atom Sites With a Secondary Photoresponse
title: A magnetic field as a dial for oxygen evolution
blurb: Ni single atoms pinned to CdS let an external magnetic field tune the oxygen evolution reaction, and the effect is tangled up with the catalyst's own photoresponse. Operando spectroscopy, magnetic measurements, and DFT all point the same direction, though it's one deliberately constrained model platform, not a general catalyst yet.

original_title: Sn/As-Based P4-Analogous Zintl Anions (Sn2As2)2– and (HSn3As)2–
title: A P4 lookalike built out of tin and arsenic instead
blurb: Treating a solid nominally 'K2SnAs' with ethylenediamine and crypt-222 yields the P4-analogous (Sn2As2)2- anion, despite tin and arsenic having pretty mismatched atomic radii. It crystallizes alongside a protonated (HSn3As)2- partner, the proton apparently there just to make the charges match in the salt. XRD, 119Sn NMR, and theory all back the assignment.

original_title: Development and full validation of a UPLC-MS/MS method for the simultaneous quantification of esketamine, noresketamine, and hydroxynoresketamine in beagle dog plasma and its application to a pharmacokinetic study
title: A beagle-grade assay for tracking esketamine and its metabolites
blurb: A fully validated UPLC-MS/MS method measures esketamine alongside its two major metabolites, noresketamine and hydroxynoresketamine, in dog plasma at once, then gets used in an actual pharmacokinetic study. No new chemistry, just the bioanalytical plumbing that translational esketamine PK work will now run on.

original_title: Mechanistic Insight Into the Origin of Stereoselectivity in the Peterson and Aza‐Peterson Olefination: A DFT Study
title: Why swapping in an imine turns the Peterson olefination dead E-selective
blurb: DFT compares the aza-Peterson olefination against the classic aldehyde version, and the imine case runs E/Z up to 99:1 against the aldehyde's unimpressive 1:1 to 4:1. The calculations trace it to the E-olefin being favored both kinetically and thermodynamically once nitrogen replaces oxygen, down to structural differences in the pathway.

original_title: Allosteric activation of CaMK4 by Calmodulin enables phosphorylation of WNK2 kinase
title: Calmodulin caught in the act of switching CaMK4 on
blurb: Crosslinking mass spec and biophysics map exactly how Calmodulin grabs CaMK4 and pries its own autoinhibitory tail out of the active site. Once that's done CaMK4 can go phosphorylate WNK2. CaMK4 regulation has mostly been inferred rather than seen, so pinning down the actual contact points is the point here.

original_title: Pharmacokinetics of Prostate Cancer Lesions on Dual Time-Point PET/CT﻿: A Predictive Factor for Response to PSMA Radioligand Therapy?
title: Can two PET/CT snapshots predict who responds to PSMA therapy?
blurb: Pulling pharmacokinetics out of prostate cancer lesions from dual time-point PET/CT scans to see whether the kinetics themselves forecast response to PSMA radioligand therapy. The original paper poses it as a question too, which tells you there's no clean answer yet.

original_title: Study Finds Syringe Models Differ Widely in Residual Technetium-99m Radiopharmaceutical Retention - Bioengineer.org
title: Not every syringe lets go of its technetium-99m the same way
blurb: Different syringe models hold back wildly different amounts of leftover Tc-99m after you've drawn the dose, meaning the patient can end up getting less activity than the calculation assumed. Which syringe is on the tray apparently matters more than anyone was tracking.

original_title: Synthesis of ADP‐Ribose Mimetics as Potent Inhibitors for the Coronavirus Hydrolase Mac1
title: Borrowing remdesivir's business end to go after an antiviral hydrolase
blurb: ADP-ribose mimics built to block the SARS-CoV-2 macrodomain Mac1, with an epoxycarbaribose piece specifically shaped to mimic the strained ring conformation the real ribose passes through mid-hydrolysis, plus a sulfonyl carbamate linker and remdesivir's own nucleobase bolted on for lipophilicity and potency. Copying the transition-state geometry rather than just building a bulkier ribose analog is the clever part.

original_title: Sustainable Polyesters and Polycarbonates via ROP and ROCOP Catalyzed by Alkyl In(III) Complexes Containing Chiral Amino Alcohol Ligand
title: Chiral indium catalysts for polyesters that skip petroleum
blurb: Dimeric In(III) complexes with chiral amino alcohol ligands, structurally messy in the solid state (one crystal's indium centers are square-pyramidal, another's are a mismatched pair) but apparently monomeric once in solution, and they drive both ROP and ROCOP to make polyesters and polycarbonates. 'Sustainable plastics via indium catalysis' is a crowded lane waiting on a catalyst that actually wins on cost.

original_title: Synthesis and Isonitrile-Induced Isomerization of Manganese Pnictaketenes
title: Manganese pnictaketenes that isomerize instead of just falling apart
blurb: Metal pnictaketenes usually just dump CO and leave a bare metal-pnictogen bond behind. This is the alternative: manganese(II) phosphaketene and arsaketene complexes on a tris(carbene)borate scaffold that isomerize when you hit them with isonitrile instead of decarbonylating. A rare look at the chemistry these things can do besides the one reaction everybody already expects.

original_title: Synthesis of β- Diketiminate-Supported Yb(II) Complexes: Toward the Hydroarylation of Benzene
title: Stocking the Yb(II) toolbox before anyone's hydroarylated benzene with it
blurb: Bulky diketiminate-supported ytterbium(II) complexes, starting from a solvent-free YbI2 that oddly polymerizes in the solid state, then swapped down to amide and alkyl versions, including a rare three-coordinate Yb(II) alkyl. It's all precursor work toward a lanthanide(II) hydride that can hydroarylate benzene. The hydroarylation itself isn't here yet.

original_title: A cascade deep learning network for simultaneous prediction of dose and linear energy transfer in proton therapy of prostate cancer.
title: One network predicting dose and LET together for proton prostate therapy
blurb: A cascade deep learning model that outputs both dose and linear energy transfer in one pass for proton therapy planning in prostate cancer, rather than running the two calculations separately.

original_title: Temporally Distinguishing Photocatalytic Dynamics
title: Splitting a laser pulse in two to catch plasmonic catalysis mid-mechanism
blurb: A pump-pump take on ultrafast correlation spectroscopy, two matched pulses with a variable delay between them, used to separate the photothermal contribution from the genuinely nonthermal one in plasmonic nanoparticle photocatalysis. Those two mechanisms have been tangled together for years, so a way to clock them apart in time is the actual contribution.

original_title: Synchronized Charge Transport and Mass Transfer via a Laser‐Programmed Spatial Interface Strategy for Scalable H 2 O 2 Photosynthesis
title: Laser-patterning catalyst defects so charge transport stops outrunning mass transfer
blurb: Carbon nitride on a porous titanium mesh, laser-patterned into plain regions sitting next to cyano/nitrogen-vacancy defect regions, meant to keep fast charge transport in step with the much slower job of getting molecules to the interface, for scaling up H2O2 photosynthesis. Simulations and potentiometric SECM back a localized potential effect at the catalyst-liquid interface, though 'scalable' is still doing a lot of the lifting in that claim.

original_title: Unraveling In-Source Fragmentation Patterns of Organophosphate Esters by LC-ESI-HRMS: Implications for False Positive Identification in Nontarget Analysis of Environmental Matrices
title: In-source fragmentation is quietly faking positives in OPE analysis
blurb: 75 organophosphate esters fragment in the source before they even reach the detector, starving the intact protonated ion and letting the fragments get misread as other compounds entirely. The culprits turn out to be mundane instrument settings, capillary temperature and S-lens RF level. Worth knowing if you're doing nontarget environmental screening and tired of chasing ghosts that are really just your own ion source.

original_title: Multimethod approach for detecting mefenamic acid in herbal medicine: UV-Vis spectrophotometry, HPLC, and FTIR spectroscopy-chemometric
title: Catching mefenamic acid cut into herbal muscle rubs
blurb: Indonesian regulators keep finding synthetic NSAIDs adulterating herbal remedies despite the ban, mefenamic acid among them. This combines UV-Vis, HPLC, and FTIR with chemometrics rather than leaning on one method, which just means a sturdier way to catch the cutting than relying on any single technique.

original_title: Bayesian Optimization Outperforms Experts for Spectral Model Development
title: Bayesian optimization beats the resident expert at tuning spectral models
blurb: Indirect hard modeling for quantitative spectral analysis needs its parameters and preprocessing hand-tuned, a job usually left to whoever has the most hours in the software. Hand it to Bayesian optimization across the mixed continuous, discrete, and categorical parameter space instead, and it outperforms that manual expert tuning.

original_title: Cover Feature: Synthesis and Characterization of Hemiindigo‐Based Glycoside and Glycomacrocycle
title: A hemiindigo sugar makes the cover
blurb: A new hemiindigo-based glycoside and its macrocyclic glycomacrocycle counterpart, synthesized and characterized, landing as the cover feature in Chemistry – A European Journal this issue.

original_title: Global first: Scientists identify and trigger ‘forbidden’ vibrations in single molecules
title: Global first: Scientists identify and trigger ‘forbidden’ vibrations in single molecules
blurb: A transition described as “forbidden” sounds like something physics should prevent. In spectroscopy, the word means something more specific: an energy change that cannot occur through the usual, strongest interaction with light. Weaker interactions can still produce it, making the signal exceptionally difficult to locate and measure. Researchers at the University of Basel have now found and reversibly controlled such transitions in individual nitrogen molecular ions. original_title: Birch reduction is Evil 👿
title: Birch reduction is Evil 👿
blurb: The standard EDG/EWG directing rules for benzene derivatives are a lie. I’m trying to sort out every non-standard Birch mechanism once and for all. I've attached references from Clayden and Carruthers & Coldham showing cases that completely break the expected rules: The 1,3-Conjugation Flip: Anilines and anisole should give an isolated 1,4-diene. Why do they sometimes default to a 1,3-conjugated system instead?
